title: Fix BuildSupersessionChains to follow multi-hop chains
description:
## G-6 (from kb-graph-rag-audit)

Despite its name, BuildSupersessionChains does not chain anything — it converts each individual Supersedes/SupersededBy edge into its own 2-element [source, target] list. A record chain `A supersedes B supersedes C` produces two disconnected pairs [A,B] and [B,C] today, never [A,B,C]. This is critical for reviewer use case: "this record was superseded, and by what, transitively."

### Detailed Steps
1. Build a directed graph from Supersedes edges only (normalize SupersededBy to same direction first)
2. Walk chains from each root (node with no incoming Supersedes edge) to its terminal leaf, emitting one ordered list per root-to-leaf path
3. Guard against cycles in supersession data — surface as data-quality warning rather than infinite-looping

### Test Plan
- 3-hop chain A→B→C produces one 3-element chain, not two 2-element pairs
- Supersession cycle (data error) is detected and reported, not looped forever
